# Reliability and Recovery Checklist: Agentic Software Engineering System: URL Shortener

**Purpose**: Validate that failure handling, rollback versus compensation, safe-stop, and resume are bounded and defined
**Created**: 2026-10-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Legend**: `[M]` mandatory (a constitution MUST, an approved requirement, or an approved decision); `[O]` optional enhancement or backlog boundary. `G0` is evaluable now against the approved specification, plan, ADRs, and contracts; `G1` is evaluable after `/speckit-tasks` and `/speckit-analyze`, before implementation. `{Detects: ...}` links an item to a failure pattern in the [README](README.md) detection matrix. Dimension tags: Completeness, Clarity, Consistency, Measurability, Coverage, Traceability, Edge Case, Assumption, Conflict, Gap.
## Classification, Retry, Fallback

- [ ] CHK001 - Are transient and permanent failures classified per plane by one classifier with stable error codes? [Completeness, Spec FR-117, Reliability §1] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK002 - Is every retried operation bounded in count, backoff, and per-attempt timeout (no unlimited retries), including resumptions? [Measurability, Spec PVT-009, PVT-010, PA-003] [M, G0] {Detects: unlimited-retries}
- [ ] CHK003 - Are retries limited to transient failures and idempotent effects, never repeating a committed non-idempotent effect? [Coverage, Spec FR-117 NAC] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK004 - Are idempotency and duplicate-execution protections defined for each repeatable operation (creation, node attempt, submission, decision, audit write)? [Coverage, Reliability §3, Constitution VIII] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK005 - Are fallbacks defined per failing capability, recorded, and prohibited from lowering any gate or policy? [Clarity, Spec FR-118] [M, G0]

## Rollback, Compensation, Safe-Stop, Resume

- [ ] CHK006 - Are rollback and compensation each defined, with the compensate-only effects listed (audit, approvals, committed code, external sends)? [Completeness, Spec DEC-056, ADR-021] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK007 - Is a rollback claim valid only for an abortable unit of work, with a rollback claim for a compensate-only effect defined as invalid? [Measurability, Spec ASM-014] [M, G0] {Detects: invalid-rollback-claim}
- [ ] CHK008 - Does every committed compensate-only effect have a defined compensation action, so a missing one is detectable? [Coverage, Spec FR-119, ADR-021] [M, G0] {Detects: missing-compensation}
- [ ] CHK009 - Is a failed compensation defined to escalate and safe-stop, never to be ignored? [Coverage, Spec FR-119 NAC, Orchestration SS-2] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK010 - Are all safe-stop triggers enumerated, with the terminal state, preserved evidence, and a prohibition on resuming SAFE_STOPPED? [Completeness, Spec FR-120, DEC-050] [M, G0] {Detects: missing-safe-stop}
- [ ] CHK011 - Is resume defined per interruption type, with restored state, effect-ledger adoption, bounded resumptions, and no duplicate effects? [Completeness, Spec FR-121, PVT-011] [M, G0] {Detects: missing-resume}
- [ ] CHK012 - Is partial failure of parallel branches defined (drain, no dependents, compensate, safe-stop)? [Coverage, Reliability §7] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK013 - Is behavior defined for unavailability of PostgreSQL, Redis, the inbox, scanners, and the clock? [Coverage, Reliability §7, Spec FR-021] [M, G0]

## Idempotency, Limitations, Evidence

- [ ] CHK014 - Is the idempotency lifecycle defined for validation rejection, transient failure, permanent failure, lease expiry, supersession, and post-retention reuse? [Completeness, Spec FR-015..FR-018, DEC-029..DEC-034] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK015 - Are LIM-001..LIM-004 disclosed with accepted rationale and the mitigation required where one exists? [Assumption, Spec Known Limitations] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK016 - Is the recovery-time target defined and measured with a stated population and exclusions? [Measurability, Spec PVT-011, Observability §5] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK017 - Is a fault-injection scenario defined for each reliability claim and marked synthetic, so no claim rests on an untested path? [Coverage, Reliability §8] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK018 - Is evidence of success, failure, retry, compensation, recovery, and latency required? [Completeness, POL-REL-003, Constitution VIII] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK019 - Are retry jitter and multi-node reliability labelled out of scope? [Coverage, ADR-020] [O, G0]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items marked `[Gap]` or `[Conflict]` name a place where the current documents are silent or disagree; they are findings for the reviewer to resolve, not pre-judged results
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items are numbered sequentially within this file (`CHK001` onward); cite them as `<file>:CHKnnn`
